Generative AI Guidelines for Students – Faculty of Mechanical Engineering



Generative AI tools (such as Copilot, ChatGPT, and Gemini) are rapidly changing how we study and work.
The following guideline outlines when and how students can use such tools within their education at the
Faculty of Mechanical Engineering, while ensuring academic integrity, personal learning, and ethical
responsibility.


AI as a Learning Support Tool

AI tools can support your learning by:
    • Explaining concepts
    • Refining language
    • Assisting with programming and debugging
    • Acting as a brainstorming partner

tools. If this is the case, you are required to add an acknowledgement** to your work.

claims.claimText: Teaching Support warns that relying on AI detectors to penalise students risks false accusations; use appropriate authenticity checks and Board procedures. This is not a university ban on detectors.

evidence.evidenceSnippet: Relying on AI-detection tools to penalise students risks false accusations, unfair treatment, and a breakdown of trust between staff and students. While plagiarism checkers help enforce clear rules, AI detectors operate in a grey area where “false positives” are common and untestable. Using them as a policing mechanism is therefore neither effective nor equitable in way of upholding assessment integrity. Instead, it is recommended that educators focus on adapting assessments to be more AI-resilient.
